newsitem.title: MEXICO: LatAm stocks seen steady, awaiting news.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen steady, awaiting news.

text.p: Investors can expect another quiet week as most Latin American stock markets are seen consolidating while awaiting political and economic developments, dealers said.

Mexican stocks are seen stable in the wake of peaceful local elections and the Federal Open Market Committee decision not to raise U.S. interest rates, although Congressional strife over a political reform bill is seen as a little unsettling.
The blue chip IPC index gained 37.47 points last week, or 1.12 percent, to close at 3,385.13.
Dealers see trade slowed down by the public holiday on Wednesday, and are looking ahead to Q3 GDP figures being released on Thursday MXAAP.

Chilean blue chips are seen soft this week on concerns that a foreign investment fund could be selling part of its portfolio, with jitters over the sales undermining the market towards the end of last week, said dealers.
But stocks could rise towards the end of the week if bargain hunters move in to take advantage of the weakness, they said.
"I think we'll see slides for a couple of days but the trend could reverse if bargain hunters move in," said one trader.
The Argentine blue-chip MerVal index rose 4.1 percent last week to 603.21 and stands 5.7 percent higher so far this month.
"The bolsa is likely to regroup a bit, with a floor of 595-600, but the fundamentals are all very strong and could push the MerVal to 620 in the near-term," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.

Brazil shares are seen steady in thin turnover with investors following developments in congress, which was expected to get back to normal this week after second-round municipal elections ended Friday.
"Stock prices are expected to remain steady with weak volume because there is no news that could lead to an uptrend in the market," a trader said.
Brokers said the market would keep a close eye on the progress of a congressional proposal that would allow presidential re-election.
Brazil shares dropped 0.5 percent last week to close at 65,229 points Thursday. Volume was thin, averaging $300 million.
Caracas share prices were seen building after a slow start to the week as the global share placement of shares in Venezuelan telephone company CANTV comes to a close, traders said.
November 21 is a key date: the offer price will be finally settled for the 289 million shares.
"The whole market is going to rise," said stock exchange President Alejandro Salcedo.
